conclusion.justification: The report explicitly states that the claim is supported, citing official FDA prescribing information and DailyMed drug labels confirming that Kyleena is approved for pregnancy prevention for up to five years.
conclusion.label: endorses

report:
**Conclusion: supported (in the United States).** Kyleena, a 19.5-mg levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system, is labeled/approved to prevent pregnancy for **up to five years**. The FDA-hosted 2023 prescribing-information label is the strongest source among the supplied evidence, and DailyMed—NLM’s official drug-label repository—states the same indication. Both specify replacement after five years if ongoing contraception is wanted.

The basis is regulatory labeling informed by clinical evaluation of the device’s contraceptive performance through its labeled duration. The supplied literature result also describes Kyleena as the first low-dose levonorgestrel IUS approved for up to five years and says clinical trials included both women who had and had not given birth. However, the retrieved snippet does not provide trial methods or pregnancy-rate figures, so it supports context rather than allowing an independent quantitative assessment of effectiveness.

“Up to five years” is a maximum labeled use period—not a guarantee that pregnancy cannot occur. It also assumes the device is correctly placed and remains in place; it should be replaced at five years for continued prevention.

Sources:  
- FDA prescribing information: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2023/208224s005lbl.pdf  
- DailyMed label: https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=2e07c155-21e1-4781-9633-ce8bddd47080  
- Clinical-review result: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40267-017-0395-9
